about: R27 review ledger (D110). One entry per safety-class Spanish string: the exact English, the exact Spanish, sha = sha256(en + U+0000 + es), and how far its review has got — draft (written), reviewed (blind second pass agreed AND back-translated to English without the original), person (a Spanish-reading crew member read it on a phone, R27 #5 / R29 #3). Safety-class Spanish is served only at reviewed or person. Editing either side without re-reviewing fails the build (src/i18n/ledger.ts ledgerProblems).

entries.es: NO LO MANEJE NI LO USE — FUERA DE SERVICIO (FRENOS O DIRECCIÓN)
entries.translatedBy: Claude — proposed in D112 (2026-10-22) after the blind review found drift in the plan table’s "NO SE MANEJA — FRENOS/DIRECCIÓN"; applied in D112’s held-five round
entries.reviewedBy: Two blind passes, 2026-10-22 (D112’s held-five round): a second translation of the English alone (never saw this Spanish) and a back-translation of this Spanish alone (never saw the English) — two agents with no tools, neither saw the other side; compared by Claude.
entries.backTranslation: DO NOT DRIVE IT OR USE IT — OUT OF SERVICE (BRAKES OR STEERING)
entries.note: Recorded 2026-10-22 (D112) — the held-five round. Back: same meaning — out of service, with the order that state puts on a crew (do not drive it or use it) and the reason (brakes or steering: the only thing that holds a unit, src/fleet/breakdown.ts, R26). Second (the English alone): "RETENIDO — FUERA DE SERVICIO" — held, out of service: the same meaning; D112’s first blind second, "NO CONDUZCA — FUERA DE SERVICIO", agrees too. Flagged and accepted: "manejar" is handle in some places — "NI LO USE" bans both readings; the brackets carry no verb and do not say which of the two failed — the English badge says neither (the Fleet card’s line names "brake/steering defect"); the order allows no short move — it errs toward stopping, and only Mike signs the unit back on; "dirección" is also address or direction — beside FRENOS and MANEJE it reads as steering. Replaces the plan’s "NO SE MANEJA — FRENOS/DIRECCIÓN" (D112: drift — it can read as a description, not an order), which is no longer in the repo.

entries.en: PERMIT LIKELY — do not start protected work until the permit is confirmed.
entries.es: PROBABLEMENTE SE NECESITA PERMISO — no empiece el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work) hasta que se confirme el permiso.
entries.translatedBy: Claude — R27 Phase A unit 1, first translation pass (D111)
entries.backTranslation: A PERMIT IS PROBABLY NEEDED — do not start the work that requires a permit (protected work) until the permit is confirmed.
entries.note: Not recorded (D112) — held again in D112’s held-five round (2026-10-22). Back (D112 and the held-five round, both blind): no drift — the hedge on the need, the prohibition firm. Flagged and accepted: "permiso" is also permission — the headline and "requiere permiso" frame it as a permit, and both forward passes chose it; "hasta que se confirme" names no one — the English names no one; "until it is confirmed whether one is needed" still stops; which work is meant — the English "protected work" asks the reader the same, and the headline says a permit is probably needed for this job; "probablemente" is the English’s own hedge, under a firm "no empiece"; the English gloss does not help a Spanish-only reader — the English line is shown beneath. Second (D112’s held-five round): "PROBABLEMENTE REQUIERE PERMISO (PERMIT LIKELY) — no comience el trabajo protegido (protected work) hasta que se confirme el permiso." Held again because the blind second translation (the English alone) wrote "el trabajo protegido (protected work)" for "protected work" — the rendering the glossary rules out (src/i18n/glossary.ts TRADE_TERMS, D111 UI 5: it reads as work done with protection, and a back-translation returns "protected work" without flagging it). Everything else in that translation means what this Spanish means, but no blind forward pass has yet agreed with "el trabajo que requiere permiso" (D111’s wrote "en zona protegida", this one "protegido"). Owed, one of: Mike rules that the glossary settles the term (then this entry can be recorded as is — its Spanish is unchanged and both rounds’ back-translations found no drift), or a blind second translation made from the English with the glossary’s trade term given.

entries.en: NO OVERLAY — VERIFY W/ CITY before protected work.
entries.es: VERIFIQUE CON LA CIUDAD — EL MAPA NO MOSTRÓ ZONA PROTEGIDA. Hágalo antes de empezar el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work).
entries.translatedBy: Claude — R27 Phase A unit 1, first translation pass (D111)
entries.backTranslation: CHECK WITH THE CITY — THE MAP DID NOT SHOW A PROTECTED ZONE. Do it before starting the work that requires a permit (protected work).
entries.note: Not recorded (D112) — held again in D112’s held-five round (2026-10-22). Back (D112 and the held-five round, both blind): no change of meaning. Flagged — the back-translator’s highest misreading risk, for Mike: the map clause can read as a finding that clears ("the map shows there is no protected zone"), and "no protected zone … the work that requires a permit" can read as "nothing here needs a permit, so nothing to verify"; there is no explicit "do not start until verified". The English "NO OVERLAY — VERIFY W/ CITY before protected work" has the same shape (and the blind second translation reproduced it), so under D112’s rule it is the English’s, not a translation drift; the Spanish leads with VERIFY, unconditionally. If the line should say the map is not a clearance, that is an English change first (Mike). Also flagged: "Hágalo" points back across the middle sentence; "la ciudad" names no office — nor does the English. Second (D112’s held-five round): "SIN CAPA DE ZONA PROTEGIDA EN EL MAPA (NO OVERLAY) — VERIFIQUE CON LA CIUDAD antes del trabajo protegido (protected work)." Held again because the blind second translation (the English alone) wrote "el trabajo protegido (protected work)" for "protected work" — the rendering the glossary rules out (src/i18n/glossary.ts TRADE_TERMS, D111 UI 5: it reads as work done with protection, and a back-translation returns "protected work" without flagging it). Everything else in that translation means what this Spanish means, but no blind forward pass has yet agreed with "el trabajo que requiere permiso" (D111’s wrote "en zona protegida", this one "protegido"). Owed, one of: Mike rules that the glossary settles the term (then this entry can be recorded as is — its Spanish is unchanged and both rounds’ back-translations found no drift), or a blind second translation made from the English with the glossary’s trade term given.

entries.note: Not recorded (D112) — held again in D112’s held-five round (2026-10-22). Back (D112 and the held-five round, both blind): no drift. Flagged and accepted: "Arbo" may be taken for a person (or "árbol") — the English says Arbo too, and either way the step is the office; "no pudo leer el chequeo" may read as an illegible document rather than a failed lookup — either way the status is unknown and the step is the same; "chequeo" is informal (D110, open for Mike); "consulte con" is check with, as the English says (L13 is recorded with it); which work is meant — as PERMIT LIKELY’s line. Second (D112’s held-five round): "ESTADO DEL PERMISO DESCONOCIDO — Arbo no pudo leer la revisión de permisos (permit screen). Consulte con la oficina antes del trabajo protegido (protected work)." Held again because the blind second translation (the English alone) wrote "el trabajo protegido (protected work)" for "protected work" — the rendering the glossary rules out (src/i18n/glossary.ts TRADE_TERMS, D111 UI 5: it reads as work done with protection, and a back-translation returns "protected work" without flagging it). Everything else in that translation means what this Spanish means, but no blind forward pass has yet agreed with "el trabajo que requiere permiso" (D111’s wrote "en zona protegida", this one "protegido"). Owed, one of: Mike rules that the glossary settles the term (then this entry can be recorded as is — its Spanish is unchanged and both rounds’ back-translations found no drift), or a blind second translation made from the English with the glossary’s trade term given.

entries.backTranslation: PERMIT CHECK NOT DONE — status UNKNOWN, there is no check on record. Check with the office before starting the work that requires a permit (protected work).
entries.note: Not recorded (D112) — held again in D112’s held-five round (2026-10-22). Back (D112 and the held-five round, both blind): no drift. Flagged and accepted: "SIN HACER" may suggest the crew does the check — the line sends them to the office before starting; "no hay chequeo registrado" does not say whether one was ever done — "no screen on file" says no more; it reads close to the UNKNOWN line — both send the crew to the office, the difference is the office’s; "consulte" as the UNKNOWN line; pending is not done (as the glossary label, recorded); which work is meant — as PERMIT LIKELY’s line. Second (D112’s held-five round): "REVISIÓN DE PERMISOS PENDIENTE (PERMIT SCREEN PENDING) — estado DESCONOCIDO, no hay revisión registrada. Consulte con la oficina antes del trabajo protegido (protected work)." Held again because the blind second translation (the English alone) wrote "el trabajo protegido (protected work)" for "protected work" — the rendering the glossary rules out (src/i18n/glossary.ts TRADE_TERMS, D111 UI 5: it reads as work done with protection, and a back-translation returns "protected work" without flagging it). Everything else in that translation means what this Spanish means, but no blind forward pass has yet agreed with "el trabajo que requiere permiso" (D111’s wrote "en zona protegida", this one "protegido").
